title: Claude rated my wordy build hint "Excellent". A player didn't
author: flockbaygames
selftext:
I asked Claude Opus 5.5 to audit my Godot game and it read the rack placement hint, "Pallet rack for $900 · R turns it · right-click to stop", and called it "Excellent feedback". Someone on Reddit saw that same hint in my trailer and said they'd seen no modern game that types this instead of using a rotate icon. The job list in the same trailer they called "Just text-vomit".

I think that's the core problem with AI-built UI. Players glance but an AI explains, so the screens it builds come out as sentences, and when you ask it to review them it reads every word, so a sentence always looks clear to it.

What worked was asking for numbers and icons instead. The job rows went from about 33 words to 9 (an icon, a count, a status chip and a time), the hint became key caps, and the buy dialog became a table. And instead of asking the AI whether a screen is clear, I ask it to count the words on it.

Has anyone found a better way to get an AI to judge UI the way a player sees it?
